title: shortburst-attention-fusion-and-slab-packing-for-short-sequence-latency
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: Many customer workloads at Redwood are dominated by short sequences (<64 tokens) where per-request overhead (kernel launch, KV cache management, micro-batch alignment) dominates token cost. This PR introduces a runtime path optimized for short-burst workloads: 1) an attention-fusion kernel variant that fuses small-sequence attention + rotary/ALiBi precompute to reduce kernel launches for sequences <= 64, 2) a token-slab packing allocator that packs multiple short requests into a single device slab with per-request offsets to avoid per-token KV allocations, and 3) a micro-continuous batching tweak that lowers the batching tick for short sequences while preserving overall throughput for long sequences. The goal is to reduce median latency for short requests without regressions for long-tail workloads. Changes: implemented fused_attention_short.cu and refactored attention dispatch to pick the fused kernel based on sequence_length and head_count thresholds; added slab_packer.{cc,h} which provides a fast arena allocator for short KV segments and a lightweight header describing offsets; introduced a new shortburst batching policy that lowers the flush timeout to 2ms for short requests and adds an adaptive cooldown to avoid microbursting on sustained high QPS; added smoke and microbench tests simulating tens of thousands of small requests. Compatibility: default behavior is conservative—the fused kernel engages only when model geometry matches supported head/hidden layouts and when quantization mode is FP16 or 4-bit fused path; slab packing is opt-in via runtime cfg short_slab_enabled=true to allow staged rollouts. Rollout plan: canary on dedicated-pool-3 for 48 hours, metric watch on median_p95_latency_shortseq, kv_allocator_misses, gpu_util; automatic rollback on error spikes. This PR also includes a short note for SDK teams to add a small-client-side retry jitter to avoid synchronized flapping. Checklist: [x] unit tests added for slab allocator and fused kernel dispatch [x] microbench harness for short-seq latency [x] docs: runtime tuning note in perf/short_seq.md [x] Linear ticket: ENG-1842.
commits: 4 commits: (1) shortburst: add fused attention kernel variant and doc comments; (2) slab: implement token slab allocator with header+offsets and wrap in RAII; (3) batching: add shortburst policy and adaptive cooldown; (4) tests/docs: microbench, unit tests, and perf note.
review_comments: Diego Martinez: Nice approach; can we add a guard for head_dim % 8 != 0 to avoid warp divergence?
Author (Ava Chen): added head_dim modulo guard and fallback to standard kernel when misaligned; microbench shows <0.5% extra overhead for those cases
Priya Kapoor: please ensure slab_packer zeroes headers for safety across reused slabs
Author (Ava Chen): headers zeroed and test added to cover reuse case
release_notes: Add short-sequence optimized attention fusion and token slab packing to reduce median latency for workloads with sequences <=64 tokens; opt-in via runtime config 'short_slab_enabled' and controlled rollout.
benchmark_summary: Canary microbench (RTX A100, FP16 weights) shows median latency for 32-token requests reduced from 8.9ms to 5.1ms (43% improvement); 95th percentile reduced from 18.3ms to 10.7ms; throughput effect on long sequences (>512) is within +-1.5%.
regression_guard: Added unit tests for allocator reuse, attention dispatch fallbacks, and integration-shortseq harness; telemetry asserts on kv_allocator_misses and kernel_selection_ratio added to prevent silent regressions.
